text: Ship's stores, sold to landsmen at landsman prices.
Twine, hooks, tar, and a barrel of ship's biscuit
that has outlasted two owners of this shop.
Vessels stacked in a rope cradle so they do not roll.
The wall behind them is still salt-stained from the
spring the harbour came up over the sill.
Lamp oil, in every size of can.
Brackwater burns a great deal of lamp oil.
The fog does not care what hour it is.
The display case, glass gone soft and wavy with age.
Tonics inside, arranged by colour rather than by use,
which the clerk insists is a system.
